name: Protocol

subjectOf.text: The more rigid an organization's structure, the more susceptible it is to corruption; at the chaos stage there is no protocol rigidity and therefore no opportunity for corruption, because with no group goal there is nothing to subvert.
subjectOf.abstract: The more rigid the structure, the more susceptible the organization is to corruption. There is no protocol rigidity at the chaos stage, so there is no opportunity for corrup- tion—since there is no group goal there is no opportunity to subvert it.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Introduction to Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782192
scope_conditions: comparison across the chaos, decentralized, and centralized stages

subjectOf.text: The study runs fixed-size replacement, the protocol on which collapse was first shown, and includes no accumulation arm, so no result it produces bears on whether a filter adds anything once real data accumulates.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: Applies to the replacement regime only.
The distinction matters because accumulating real and synthetic data keeps error bounded in the settings studied, while replacement collapses.
